rationale: C11 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template for the child. Both are Kennedy letters about improving unemployment insurance, and both use the same linked rationale: benefits relieve workers and families while stabilizing the broader economy through purchasing power during recessions. The child also refers directly to improvements previously recommended to Congress, matching C11's proposed permanent improvements. C22 is a strong secondary parallel concerning temporary unemployment compensation and purchasing power, while C05 shares the economic-recovery and purchasing-power framing but concerns social security more generally.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The $28 billion that has been paid out in benefits ... has eased the financial burden of many millions of workers who lost their jobs through no fault of their own.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Enactment of the draft bill will to some extent alleviate the suffering of unemployed workers and their families
shared_material.explanation: Both describe unemployment benefits as direct relief for unemployed workers and their families.

shared_material.child_excerpt: It has also contributed materially to lessening the impact of economic downturns on business by providing essential purchasing power for our economy.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: will help stabilize the economy by increasing the purchasing power of such workers
shared_material.explanation: This is a close and distinctive shared causal formulation connecting unemployment compensation, purchasing power, and macroeconomic stabilization.

shared_material.child_excerpt: it has also lightened and shortened the recessions we have experienced during the past 25 years.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: a Federal program of additional compensation, on a stand-by basis, for workers who exhaust their regular benefits during economic recessions
shared_material.explanation: Both specifically frame unemployment insurance as machinery for addressing recessions.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The contribution that the unemployment insurance program has made to the nation over the years points up the desirability of the improvements in the program I have recommended to the Congress.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: a bill which would provide permanent improvements to the Federal-State unemployment compensation system
shared_material.explanation: The child's appeal for previously recommended improvements closely tracks C11's permanent-improvement proposal.
